title: RUML-EXT — RUML Capability Extension Sidecar
description: JSON-based sidecar format carrying capability extension data for a RUML file without modifying it. Bound to the exact base file version via `$base` (id + hash).

$format.description: Format discriminator identifying this as a RUML-EXT sidecar

$specVersion.description: RUML spec version this sidecar conforms to

$base.description: Reference to the base RUML file (id + hash)

capabilities.description: The capabilities whose data this EXT file carries, in order; root-level artifact data travels in each entry's `payload` (§4.2), never as separate root fields (CAP-23)

nodes.description: Extension data for base nodes, indexed by node UUID

allOf.title: CAP-23 — prohibited root fields
allOf.description: `metadata` and `rulemap` belong exclusively to the base RUML file and MUST NOT appear in an EXT root. Listed explicitly (although the root is closed) so the violation is reported by name.

allOf.title: §4.5 — node keys are declared capabilities
allOf.description: Node extension keys MUST be capability ids from this file's root `capabilities`. Only the degenerate case is expressible here: with no declared capabilities, no node may carry any extension data. The general membership check is a parser obligation.

BaseReference.description: Reference to the base RUML file this sidecar extends (§4.5). `id` is the base file's `metadata.id`; `hash` pins the exact version of the base file the extension data was written against. A parser MUST match both against the base file before merging (CAP-24).

id.description: The `metadata.id` of the base RUML file

hash.description: Integrity hash of the base RUML file at the time this EXT file was created (`<algorithm>:<hex>`)

ExtensionNodes.description: Extension data indexed by the UUID (`id` field) of the base node — not by lexId, because lexIds are not position-unique for modular nodes (§4.5). Every UUID MUST resolve to a node of the base RUML file (CAP-26); that lookup is a parser obligation.

NodeExtension.description: Node-level capability payloads for one base node, keyed by capability id (§4.5). Every key MUST be a capability declared in the root `capabilities` array of this EXT file, and the same capability MUST NOT also be carried inline by the base node (CAP-27); both are parser obligations. Official ids route to the same node-level payload shapes as inline node capabilities (§4.3).

ruml:protocol.description: ruml:protocol has no node-level data (§4.13) and MUST NOT appear on a node

additionalProperties.description: Payload of a `ruml:draft/…`, third-party, or unrouted official capability; everything here belongs to the capability

DatapointDateTime.description: Date and time of day for a datapoint: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, optionally with seconds, a fraction of a second and an offset (§4.7.1, §4.7.3)

DatapointTime.description: Time of day without a date: HH:MM, optionally with seconds, a fraction of a second and an offset (§4.7.1, §4.7.3)

Capabilities.description: Declared capabilities, in order (§4.2); the order is significant

OfficialCapabilityId.description: Official RUML capability id in the reserved `ruml:` namespace.

DraftCapabilityId.description: Local draft capability id (e.g. `ruml:draft/my-capability`). Used for in-progress capabilities.

ReverseDomainCapabilityId.description: Third-party capability id in reverse-domain form (e.g. `com.example/my-capability`).

description.description: Description of what the datapoint represents

unit.description: Unit of the value; required for type 'currency', otherwise only applicable to types 'number' and 'percentage'

sensitive.description: Whether the datapoint holds sensitive/personal data

format.description: Format refining the type (e.g. taxId for identifier)

options.description: Allowed options; required and non-empty for type 'enum'

binding.description: How the datapoint value is sourced (input, external or computed). `type` selects the kind; each kind's own properties are listed under `allOf`, as capability entries do (§4.2).

type.description: Binding kind: `input` is supplied by the user, `external` is fetched from a source, `computed` is derived from other datapoints

hint.description: Hint shown to the user when entering the value

placeholder.description: Placeholder text for the input field

defaultValue.description: Default value pre-filled for the input

ref.description: Symbolic reference to the external source

sourceType.description: Kind of external source the value is fetched from

fallback.description: Input binding used when the external source cannot be reached

type.description: Binding kind: the value is supplied by user input

hint.description: Hint shown to the user when entering the value

placeholder.description: Placeholder text for the input field

defaultValue.description: Default value pre-filled for the input

expression.description: JSONata expression; other datapoints are referenced by their id

description.description: Description of the external source or of the calculation

validation.description: Validation rules applied to the datapoint value

required.description: Whether a value must be provided

min.description: Minimum value (number, or ISO-8601 string for temporal types)

max.description: Maximum value (number, or ISO-8601 string for temporal types)

pattern.description: Regular expression the value must match

set.description: The set this datapoint instantiates; required when type is object, not applicable to other types

cardinality.description: Repetition of the object; absent means a single object. Only applicable to type 'object'

allOf.title: §4.7.4 — an object datapoint instantiates a set

uri.description: URI of the text as published by its source (see the URI convention in §4.12); omitted for texts written in the RUML file itself

timestamp.description: When the author retrieved and recorded this text

type.description: How the text content is carried; 'external' is deprecated

text.description: Plain text; for embedded texts with status 'inForce', exactly one of text and content is required

content.description: Structured text in RUML Text form (§4.12)

digest.description: SHA3-256 over the RFC 8785 form of content; required with content

source.description: Provenance of content: the source document it was imported from

url.description: URL of the text; required for type 'url'

containerPath.description: Path to the text inside the RUML container; required for type 'container'

isReferenced.description: Whether the text is referenced by at least one node

uri.description: URI of the source document the content was imported from

digest.description: Digest of the archived source document

terms.description: URI of the source's reuse terms, where the source attaches any

RumlTextName.description: Element or attribute name as in the XML, optionally with a prefix declared by an xmlns:<prefix> attribute in scope

RumlTextAttrs.description: Attributes of an element, keyed by (prefixed) name

RumlTextRootAttrs.description: Attributes of the root element; xmlns declares the dialect's namespace as the default namespace

xmlns.description: Namespace URI of the text's Akoma Ntoso dialect, e.g. http://Inhaltsdaten.LegalDocML.de/1.8.2/

RumlTextNode.description: One element of the Akoma Ntoso tree

RumlTextDocument.description: Root of a RUML Text document: the Akoma Ntoso root element, declaring the dialect's namespace as its default namespace (§4.12)

TextAnchor.description: Points at a text of this RUML's own ruml:text-reference data, or at one element of it (§4.12)

id.description: Key of the text entry in this RUML's own data

element.description: GUID of an element of the entry's RUML Text; omitted for the whole text

type.description: represents: the norm the node implements (at most one per node); refers-to: a text the node refers to
How the context content is carried

timestamp.description: Modification time of the context in ISO 8601 format

subject.description: Whether this context is the subject of the evaluation

source.description: Free-form description of the context source

url.description: URL of the context; required for type 'url'

containerPath.description: Path to the context inside the RUML container; required for type 'container'

accessDate.description: Date the context url was last accessed

expression.description: JSONata expression computing the node's truth value

description.description: Optional explanation of what the expression evaluates
Description of the actions declared for the node

onTrue.description: Action to run when the node evaluates to true

onFalse.description: Action to run when the node evaluates to false

onUndefined.description: Action to run when the node evaluates to undefined

ref.description: Symbolic reference to the operation implementation

config.description: Optional, runtime-defined configuration for the action

refs.description: Ids of root-level context entries referenced by the node

model.description: Symbolic reference to the AI model, resolved by the tool at runtime

description.description: Description of what the query determines

inputs.description: Inputs (context, datapoints, texts) supplied to the query

context.description: Context entries supplied as input to the query

id.description: Id of the referenced context entry

role.description: Role the context plays in the query (reference or subject)

dataPoints.description: Ids of datapoints supplied as input to the query

texts.description: Ids of texts supplied as input to the query

deterministic.description: Whether the query should be evaluated deterministically

effort.description: Effort the model should spend on the query (low, medium, high)

temperature.description: Sampling temperature for the query, between 0 and 1

refs.description: Anchors into this RUML's own texts; at most one of type represents

NodeAnchor.description: Absolute anchor to a node of one version of another RUML file (§4.15): `<ruml-version-uri>#node/<id>`. Same-document anchors (`#node/…`) are not node anchors.

NodeRef.description: A reference to a node of another RUML file (§4.15).

TreeRefs.description: Node payload of ruml:tree-reference (§4.15): references to nodes of other RUML files.

represents.description: The node of another RUML file this node stands for.

refersTo.description: Nodes of other RUML files this node refers to.

TreeInclude.description: Node payload of ruml:tree-include (§4.16): the node of another RUML file whose subtree is evaluated in place of this leaf.

DatapointSet.description: A reusable structured type: a named group of datapoints (§4.7.4)

fields.description: Member datapoints, keyed by datapoint id; a field may itself be type: object (nesting)

data.description: Datapoint definitions, keyed by datapoint id

sets.description: Reusable structured types, keyed by set id

data.description: Text definitions, keyed by text id (text_…)
Context entries, keyed by context id (ctx_…)

config.description: Root-level configuration for the AI query capability

systemPrompt.description: System prompt applied to all AI queries in the document

CapabilityEntry.description: A declared capability (§4.2). Order is significant.

payload.description: Capability-defined content; everything here belongs to the capability

required.description: Whether the capability must be resolved to evaluate the file

role.description: The role the rulemap expects a non-official capability to play (§4.1). Official `ruml:` ids have a fixed role and MUST NOT declare one; every other id MUST declare it. A parser that implements the capability MUST reject a role that differs from its implementation. `decision` decides a leaf, `combiner` decides a node from its children.

allOf.title: CAP-05 — an official capability does not declare its role
allOf.description: The role of a `ruml:` capability is fixed by its chapter; only a non-official id declares one.

allOf.title: CAP-03 — a non-official capability declares its role
allOf.description: A `ruml:draft/` or reverse-domain capability has no role in this specification; its root entry states the role the rulemap expects.

UniqueOfficialCapabilityIds.description: Each official `ruml:` capability id may appear at most once (§4.2, CAP-10). Only the `ruml:` ids defined by this spec version can be constrained here; duplicate `ruml:draft/…` and reverse-domain ids that differ in payload are not detectable in JSON Schema and MUST be rejected by the parser.
